question_prompt:
N01 — High-Alkalinity BWRO: Minimum Passing Acid Dose

An inland BWRO plant operates at a fixed 70% recovery. Calcite and Dolomite control the concentrate risk, while sulfate scales are safe. The site cannot dispose of softener regenerant but permits RO-feed pH down to 6.10. Use equilibrate_feed to choose among acidification, softening and other pretreatment, and identify the minimum passing HCl dose on a 0.001 mol/s grid.

reference_answer:
N01 — Stepwise Gold Answer: High-Alkalinity BWRO: Minimum Passing Acid Dose

The efficient reference trajectory uses 4 equilibrate_feed calls: zero-dose diagnosis, mechanism-based counterfactual pruning, then adjacent fail/pass points or a stated guarantee envelope to lock the stopping boundary. Other reasonable orders are acceptable if the information gain of each call is explained.

Recommend HCl acidification alone at 0.016 mol/s. It gives Calcite SI=-0.18827, Dolomite SI=-0.49365, Gypsum SI=-0.60720 and equilibrium pH=6.108. At 0.015 mol/s, Calcite SI=-0.09827 narrowly misses the -0.10 margin; at 0.018 mol/s, pH falls to 5.988. The selected dose equals about 2,100.10 g/h pure HCl or 6.087 L/h of 30 wt% HCl at 1.15 kg/L. Softening is rejected by the regenerant-disposal constraint.
